subject: Franska 4
title: The conditional and si-clauses
sourceSummary: The conditionnel présent and passé, plus the three types of si-clauses for real, hypothetical, and counterfactual conditions.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Si j'avais le temps, j'___ au cinéma." (aller = to go)
questions.opener: "Si + imperfect" in the subordinate clause is always matched by the same tense in the main clause.
questions.explanation: For hypothetical conditions in the present, the pattern is "si + imparfait, ... conditionnel présent". "Aller" in the conditionnel présent for "je" is "irais": "Si j'avais le temps, j'irais au cinéma" (if I had time, I would go to the cinema).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Si tu ___ tes devoirs plus tôt, tu ne serais pas stressé maintenant." (faire = to do)
questions.opener: The main clause is in the conditionnel présent — which tense does the si-clause take then?
questions.explanation: This is a mixed conditional sentence: a past cause ("if you had done") produces a present-day consequence ("you wouldn't be stressed now"). The si-clause takes the plus-que-parfait: "Si tu avais fait tes devoirs plus tôt, tu ne serais pas stressé maintenant."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Si j'avais su, je ne ___ pas venu(e)." (venir = to come)
questions.opener: A counterfactual condition in the past — what would have happened if things had been different.
questions.explanation: The pattern for a past, counterfactual condition is "si + plus-que-parfait, ... conditionnel passé". The conditionnel passé of "venir" is formed with "être" in the conditionnel présent + past participle: "je ne serais pas venu(e)" (I would not have come).

questions.prompt: Which form of "pouvoir" fills the gap? "___ -vous m'aider, s'il vous plaît ?"
questions.opener: A polite request is often expressed with the conditional rather than the present tense.
questions.explanation: The conditionnel présent is used for polite requests, just like "would you be able to" in English. "Pouvoir" has an irregular stem in the conditional/future: "pourr-". "Pourriez-vous m'aider ?" (would you be able to help me?) sounds more polite than "Pouvez-vous...".

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes a real/likely condition in the future?
questions.opener: One of these options uses "si + present", which signals a realistic condition rather than a hypothetical one.
choices: Si tu étudiais davantage, tu réussirais.
Si tu avais étudié, tu aurais réussi.
Si tu étudies ce week-end, tu réussiras l'examen.
Si tu avais étudié davantage, tu réussirais.
questions.explanation: "Si + présent, ... futur simple" describes a realistic condition: "Si tu étudies ce week-end, tu réussiras l'examen" (if you study this weekend, you'll pass the exam). The other examples are hypothetical (imparfait/conditionnel) or counterfactual (plus-que-parfait).

questions.prompt: How is the conditionnel présent formed for regular verbs?
questions.opener: Think of it as a blend of two other tenses you already know.
choices: The past participle + être conjugated in the present
questions.explanation: The conditionnel présent is formed with the same stem as the futur simple (usually the infinitive) plus the imperfect endings: parler → je parlerais, tu parlerais, il parlerait. The irregular future/conditional stems (être → ser-, avoir → aur-, faire → fer-) apply here too.

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "Si j'aurais gagné à la loterie, j'aurais acheté une maison."
questions.opener: "Si" can never be directly followed by the conditional — which tense should stand there instead?
questions.answer: Si j'avais gagné à la loterie, j'aurais acheté une maison.
steps: A common mistake among Swedish speakers is to put the conditional right after "si", since Swedish uses "skulle" (would) in both clauses ("om jag skulle ha vunnit...").
In French, "si" can NEVER be followed by the conditional or the future. For a counterfactual condition in the past, the si-clause must be in the plus-que-parfait: "j'aurais gagné" → "j'avais gagné".
The main clause keeps the conditionnel passé because it describes the hypothetical consequence: "j'aurais acheté une maison" (I would have bought a house).
The full correct sentence: "Si j'avais gagné à la loterie, j'aurais acheté une maison" (if I had won the lottery, I would have bought a house).

questions.prompt: What are the three types of si-clauses, and which tenses pair up in each?
questions.opener: Three patterns, three degrees of reality.
questions.answer: 1) Real/likely condition: si + présent, ... futur simple (Si tu viens, je serai content). 2) Hypothetical condition in the present/future: si + imparfait, ... conditionnel présent (Si j'avais le temps, j'irais). 3) Counterfactual condition in the past: si + plus-que-parfait, ... conditionnel passé (Si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu). Remember: "si" is NEVER followed by the future or the conditional, only by the présent, imparfait, or plus-que-parfait. Mixed sentences also occur: a past cause (plus-que-parfait) can produce a present-day consequence (conditionnel présent).
